partnershipPlan: Two residents nominated by the residents' association and one faculty assessor review the interview guide before piloting and read the draft themes for recognisability before the committee report.
socialListening: No social media listening; anonymous comments from the last two annual resident surveys about assessment are read to sensitise the guide.

items.theme: The quota at the end of the rotation
items.quote: Composite paraphrase (resident): In the last week I stop learning and start collecting; I send the same request to four people and hope two answer.
items.implication: Ask about the timing of requests across the rotation, not only the total.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase (assessor): The useful part was the two minutes at the bedside; the form comes a week later and says less.
items.implication: Explore whether the form could record the conversation rather than replace it.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase (resident): After a bad night I would never ask for an assessment on that case, even though that is where I needed feedback.
items.implication: Probe for avoided assessments and what would make them safe to request.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase (programme administrator): I send reminders about numbers every Friday; nobody asks me whether the comments say anything.
items.implication: Include administrators, whose monitoring may reinforce the quota.

summary: Four composite voices on end-of-rotation collecting, lost conversations, avoided assessments and quota monitoring.
